description: Two digital noise generators running one algorithm each from a library of banks, with a resonant filter on each, plus a third section of grit and white noise

params.text: Moves the first of the two parameters the current algorithm exposes; what it changes depends on which algorithm is loaded
Moves the second of the two parameters the current algorithm exposes; what it changes depends on which algorithm is loaded
Sets the cutoff of that section's filter, from 5.8Hz to 11800Hz
Sets the resonance of that section's filter, raising its Q from 0.7 up to about 11
Attenuates the cutoff CV for that section, squared so the bottom of the travel is fine-grained
Picks that section's filter type: lowpass, bandpass or highpass
Turning it steps through the algorithms of the current bank; a click swaps which of the two sections it edits, and a hold of half a second switches it to stepping through banks instead
Sets the density of the gritty noise, from 0.1 events per second up to 20000
Sets the resonance of the filter on the noise section, raising its Q from 0.5 up to about 20
Sets the cutoff of the filter on the noise section, from 8.2Hz to 22050Hz
Picks which noise the filter takes: the gritty noise or the white noise

inputs.text: Moves the first algorithm parameter for that section, -10V to 10V covering the whole range, and is added to the X knob
Moves the second algorithm parameter for that section, -10V to 10V covering the whole range, and is added to the Y knob
Shifts that section's filter cutoff, scaled by that section's cutoff CV attenuator
Steps through the programs of the current bank for that section, half a volt per program, counted on from the program already chosen
Shifts the density of the gritty noise, -10V to 10V covering the whole range, and is added to the grit knob
Shifts the cutoff of the filter on the noise section, scaled by that section's cutoff CV attenuator

outputs.text: That section's noise algorithm through its filter, soft-clipped and reaching 10V peak to peak
Sparse random impulses whose density the grit knob sets, reaching 10V peak to peak
Either the gritty noise or the white noise through a resonant filter, with an asymmetric saturation adding even harmonics
White noise, reaching 10V peak to peak

notes: some algorithm names in the Program A and Program B menus are greyed out and cannot be chosen: those algorithms are listed in the banks but not implemented here.
menu: Program A — picks the algorithm the A section runs, by name, from Bank 1: Textures, Bank 2: HH Clusters, Bank 3: Harsh & Wild or Bank 4: Test
Remove DC — takes the DC offset out of all three outputs; on by default
Program B — picks the algorithm the B section runs, by name, from Bank 1: Textures, Bank 2: HH Clusters, Bank 3: Harsh & Wild or Bank 4: Test
Bypass Filters — passes the raw noise with no filtering; off by default
